extraction.note: The attack line "spin and statistics for interacting fields: replace the Jost-point import by a premise the series already holds, or record modular covariance of the wedge algebras as one", nonperturbative side. The weakest modular premise known to give the spin-statistics connection is Kuckert's (1995, read in the arXiv text): the modular conjugation of the wedge algebra acts on the local algebras as the wedge's P1T reflection; full modular covariance (Guido-Longo) implies it. What is written here is the spacetime-algebra form of the geometric half of Kuckert's argument: the reflection is conjugation by the wedge's own boost bivector, whose factorisation as PT after the dual-plane turn is the stored modular-period result (ii); the reflections of the wedge and its quarter-turned copy compose to a rotor of square -1 whatever the signs of the versors (along the turned wedges the lift by continuity reaches -1 at the causal complement); and the standard Klein twist, written with i = I4, squares to the grading. The positivity the theorem needs is the spectrum condition of the interacting net, part of its hypotheses; (N+) is posed for quasi-free states of a CAR mode algebra and does not supply it. Under the spectrum condition Borchers' theorem gives the action of the modular objects on translations; nothing in the store gives their action on the local algebras, which remains the premise; (HS) and (HD) do not bear on it. Kill condition registered before computing: the product of the reflections of W' and W not equal to the lift -1 of the 2 pi rotation, or the twist with I4 not squaring to the grading; neither fired. Transport-absent: the theorem is standard, and the dual-plane reading and the unit I4 in the twist re-express it, as the stored modular-period result classifies its own I4 reading.

levels.formal:
Units and signature of the store; $\Cl(1,3)$, $I_{4} = \gamma_{0}\gamma_{1}\gamma_{2}\gamma_{3}$; $W = \{x : x^{1} > |x^{0}|\}$, its boost bivector $B = \gamma_{0}\gamma_{1}$, edge null directions $n_{\pm} = \pm\gamma_{0} + \gamma_{1}$ and dual plane $D = I_{4}B = \gamma_{2}\gamma_{3}$; $\mathrm{Ad}(V)x = VxV^{-1}$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(The wedge reflection; proved.)} $B^{2} = 1$, $B\tilde B = -1$, and $\mathrm{Ad}(B)$ is the reflection $j_{W}$: $(x^{0}, x^{1}) \mapsto (-x^{0}, -x^{1})$, $x^{2}$, $x^{3}$ fixed. Since $I_{4}D = -B$, $\mathrm{Ad}(B) = \mathrm{Ad}(I_{4}) \circ \mathrm{Ad}(D)$: the PT inversion after the turn by $\pi$ in the dual plane, which is the half modular period on values by \claimref{synthesis.modular-period-on-values-is-the-dual-plane-turn}(ii). This is the geometric part of the Bisognano-Wichmann conjugation, CPT composed with the turn by $\pi$ about the boost axis (Fact \claimref{angle.imported-theorems-deliver-their-hypotheses}).
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Edge translations; geometric part proved, modular action imported.)} $j_{W}$ reverses $n_{\pm}$ and fixes $\gamma_{2}$, $\gamma_{3}$; the wedge's boosts map $W$ into itself and dilate $n_{\pm}$ by reciprocal factors ($(5 + 4B)/3$: $n_{+} \mapsto n_{+}/9$, $n_{-} \mapsto 9n_{-}$). Under the spectrum condition, Borchers' theorem (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-kuckert-modular-pct-spin-statistics-and-borchers-theorem}(ii)) gives that the modular group of every wedge algebra (with the vacuum cyclic and separating) acts on the translations as the wedge's boosts at rapidity $-2\pi t$ and its modular conjugation as $j_{W}$, for interacting nets as well.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Turned wedges; proved.)} Independently of signs: for $B_{\pi/2} = \gamma_{0}\gamma_{2}$, the reflection versor of the quarter-turned wedge, $(\pm B_{\pi/2}\cdot\pm B)^{2} = -1$, so the two reflections compose to a rotor representing the half turn whose square is the rotation by $2\pi$ in the spin group. For the wedge $W_{\theta}$ turned by $\theta$ in the plane $\gamma_{1}\gamma_{2}$, $B_{\theta} = \gamma_{0}(\cos\theta\,\gamma_{1} + \sin\theta\,\gamma_{2})$ and $B_{\theta}B = \cos\theta + \sin\theta\,\gamma_{1}\gamma_{2}$, the spin rotor of the turn by $2\theta$; $\theta \mapsto B_{\theta}B$ runs from $1$ to $-1$ on $[0, \pi]$, $W_{\pi} = W'$ and $B_{\pi} = -B$. As maps $\mathrm{Ad}(B_{\pi}) = \mathrm{Ad}(B)$; the sign $B_{\pi} = -B$ is the lift by continuity along $\theta$, and along that lift the product of the reflection versors of $W'$ and $W$ is the rotation by $2\pi$ of the spin group, $-1$ on spinor values and $(-1)^{2s}$ on spin-$s$ values.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(The twist with the unit $I_{4}$; proved, the standard Klein-twist identity with $i$ written as $I_{4}$.)} For an even involution $k$ commuting with $I_{4}$, $V = (1 + I_{4}k)(1 + I_{4})^{-1}$ satisfies $VV^{*} = 1$, $Vk = kV$, $V^{2} = k$, and a conjugate-linear $J$ reversing $I_{4}$ and fixing $k$ has $JV^{*}J = V$, so $VJV^{*}J = k$.
\item[(v)] \emph{(Spin-statistics; imported, conditional.)} If the spectrum condition holds and the modular conjugation of the wedge algebra of the observables acts on the local algebras as $j_{W}$ (modular P1CT symmetry), with covering-group covariance, the spectrum condition, a unique vacuum, dimension at least $1 + 2$ and a compact group of internal symmetries, then for every covariant normal field the rotation by $2\pi$ equals the Bose-Fermi grading, $R(2\pi) = J_{W'}J_{W} = VJV^{*}J = k$ (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-kuckert-modular-pct-spin-statistics-and-borchers-theorem}(i), \cite{Kuckert1995}, Corollaries 3.2 and 3.5; there twisted duality is derived, from \cite{DoplicherRoberts1990}, not assumed); (iii) is the geometric step and (iv) the algebraic step in the spacetime algebra. Modular covariance (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-free-field-spin-statistics-and-guido-longo-theorem}(iii)) implies the premise.
\item[(vi)] \emph{(What remains; argued.)} The spectrum condition, a hypothesis of the theorem, gives by (ii) the action of the modular objects on translations; (N$_{+}$) is posed for quasi-free states of a CAR mode algebra (\claimref{synthesis.positive-null-energy-gives-r-premises}) and does not supply the spectrum condition of an interacting net. Nothing in the store gives the action of the modular conjugations on the local algebras, which is the remaining premise for interacting fields; (HS) and (HD) do not bear on it. Electric charge is not localisable in spacelike cones, so for the charged fields of QED the conclusion needs more than this premise.
\end{enumerate}
levels.technical:
The geometric side of the modular route to spin and statistics has a short form in the spacetime algebra. The reflection of a wedge, which reverses time and the wedge's spatial direction, is conjugation by the wedge's own boost bivector $B$; by the stored dual-plane result it is the PT inversion after the half modular period on values. The reflections of a wedge and of its quarter-turned copy compose, whatever signs the versors carry, to a rotor whose square is $-1$, the rotation by $2\pi$ in the spin group; along the turned wedges the product is $\cos\theta + \sin\theta\,\gamma_{1}\gamma_{2}$, whose lift by continuity reaches $-1$ at the causal complement. With the unit $I_{4}$ the Klein twist $V = (1 + I_{4}k)/(1 + I_{4})$ squares to the grading $k$. These are the two steps of Kuckert's theorem (standard): if each wedge's modular conjugation acts on the local algebras as the wedge's reflection, a premise weaker than modular covariance, then the rotation by $2\pi$ is the grading for interacting fields.

The spectrum condition, a hypothesis of that theorem, gives through Borchers' theorem the action of the modular objects on translations; the reflection reverses the edge's null translations and the boosts dilate them. Nothing in the store gives their action on the local algebras, which is what remains; the null ground-state premise of the horizons is posed for free (quasi-free) states and does not supply the spectrum condition of an interacting net. It does not reach electric charge, which the Gauss law keeps out of spacelike cones.
levels.lay: One way to explain why matter particles obey the exclusion rule and force particles do not uses a natural flow of the vacuum restricted to a wedge-shaped region of spacetime. In the series' algebra, the mirror image of such a wedge is a single algebraic element, the wedge's own boost plane, and mirroring twice in wedges turned by half a turn gives a full turn, which for a spin-one-half value is a sign change. If the vacuum's natural mirror operation matches the geometric mirror on every region, the spin rule follows for interacting particles. Positive energy gives that match for shifts along light rays, not for every region, and nothing in the series gives it for regions, so that match remains an assumption.
levels.one-liner: The wedge reflection is $\mathrm{Ad}(B)$, PT after the half modular period; the reflections of a wedge and its quarter-turned copy compose, for either signs of the versors, to a rotor of square $-1$ (the $2\pi$ rotation in the spin group); the $I_{4}$ twist squares to the grading; so under the spectrum condition, geometric wedge modular conjugations (weaker than modular covariance) give interacting spin-statistics by Kuckert's theorem, and nothing in the store supplies their action on the local algebras.

proofs.main:
\emph{Setting.} $\Cl(1,3)$ with $\gamma_{0}^{2} = 1$, $\gamma_{i}^{2} = -1$, $I_{4} = \gamma_{0}\gamma_{1}\gamma_{2}\gamma_{3}$, $I_{4}^{2} = -1$, $\tilde I_{4} = I_{4}$. For a versor $V$ with $V\tilde V$ a nonzero scalar, $V^{-1} = \tilde V/(V\tilde V)$ and $\mathrm{Ad}(V)x = VxV^{-1}$ preserves $Q$. The wedge is $W = \{x^{1} > |x^{0}|\}$, $B = \gamma_{0}\gamma_{1}$, $D = I_{4}B$.

\emph{(i).} $B^{2} = \gamma_{0}\gamma_{1}\gamma_{0}\gamma_{1} = -\gamma_{0}^{2}\gamma_{1}^{2} = 1$ and $\tilde B = -B$, so $B\tilde B = -1$ and $B^{-1} = B$: $B$ is a versor of the full spin group outside the identity component. $B$ anticommutes with $\gamma_{0}$ and $\gamma_{1}$ and commutes with $\gamma_{2}$, $\gamma_{3}$, so $\mathrm{Ad}(B)$ negates $x^{0}$, $x^{1}$ and fixes $x^{2}$, $x^{3}$: it is $j_{W}$, and it maps $W$ to $\{x^{1} < -|x^{0}|\}$, the causal complement $W'$. Next $D = I_{4}\gamma_{0}\gamma_{1} = \gamma_{2}\gamma_{3}$ (moving $\gamma_{0}\gamma_{1}$ through), $D^{2} = -1$, so $\mathrm{Ad}(D)$ is the turn by $\pi$ in the plane $\gamma_{2}\gamma_{3}$, and $\mathrm{Ad}(I_{4})x = -x$ for every vector since $I_{4}$ anticommutes with vectors. As $I_{4}D = I_{4}^{2}B = -B$, $\mathrm{Ad}(B) = \mathrm{Ad}(I_{4}D) = \mathrm{Ad}(I_{4}) \circ \mathrm{Ad}(D)$. That the turn by $\pi$ in the dual plane is the boost continued over half a modular period, differing from it by $x \mapsto -x$ on vectors, is \claimref{synthesis.modular-period-on-values-is-the-dual-plane-turn}(ii), cited, not re-proved. The Bisognano-Wichmann conjugation of a Wightman field is CPT composed with the turn by $\pi$ about the boost axis, acting on spacetime as $j_{W}$ (Fact \claimref{angle.imported-theorems-deliver-their-hypotheses}); (i) gives its geometric part as PT after the dual-plane turn. The script checks every identity and the action on three vectors.

\emph{(ii).} The geometric part is proved here and the modular action is imported. $Bn_{\pm} = \mp n_{\pm}$ with $n_{\pm} = \pm\gamma_{0} + \gamma_{1}$, so $\mathrm{Ad}(B)n_{\pm} = -n_{\pm}$; $\gamma_{2}$, $\gamma_{3}$ are fixed. For the boost rotor $R = \cosh(\eta/2) + B\sinh(\eta/2)$, $R n_{\pm}\tilde R = R^{2}n_{\pm} = e^{\mp\eta}n_{\pm}$, checked exactly at $R = (5 + 4B)/3$ ($R\tilde R = 1$, $e^{\eta} = 9$), and $R$ maps a point of $W$ into $W$. The translations by $a n_{+}$ and $a n_{-}$, $a \ge 0$, map $W$ into itself ($x^{1} + a > |x^{0} \pm a|$ when $x^{1} > |x^{0}|$). Under the spectrum condition (the generators of the future null translations are positive) and if the vacuum is cyclic and separating for the wedge algebra $M$, Borchers' theorem \cite{Borchers1992} (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-kuckert-modular-pct-spin-statistics-and-borchers-theorem}(ii); its modular-group form also in Fact \claimref{angle.imported-theorems-deliver-their-hypotheses}) gives $\Delta^{I_{4}t}U(a)\Delta^{-I_{4}t} = U(e^{-2\pi t}a)$ and $JU(a)J = U(-a)$ (the Hilbert space's scalars read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$, the unit of (iv), as the Fact now states it) on each half-sided translation group; the transverse translations map $M$ onto itself and fix the vacuum, so they commute with $\Delta$ and $J$. Hence the modular objects act on all translations as the boost at rapidity $-2\pi t$ and as $j_{W}$, which is the geometric action of (i) and (ii); nothing in the argument uses free fields. The spectrum condition of the interacting net is a hypothesis here (Kuckert's Assumption I); the store's (N$_{+}$) is posed for quasi-free states of a CAR mode algebra on horizon generators (\claimref{synthesis.positive-null-energy-gives-r-premises}) and does not supply it. The conjugation half of Borchers' theorem is cited from memory.

\emph{(iii).} Let $R_{\theta} = a + b\gamma_{1}\gamma_{2}$ with $a^{2} + b^{2} = n$; $R_{\theta}\tilde R_{\theta} = n$ and $\mathrm{Ad}(R_{\theta})$ turns $\gamma_{1}$ toward $\gamma_{2}$ by $\theta$ with $\cos\theta = (a^{2} - b^{2})/n$, $\sin\theta = 2ab/n$. Since $\gamma_{0}$ commutes with $\gamma_{1}\gamma_{2}$, $B_{\theta} = R_{\theta}B\tilde R_{\theta}/n = \gamma_{0}(\cos\theta\,\gamma_{1} + \sin\theta\,\gamma_{2})$, the boost bivector of $W_{\theta} = \mathrm{Ad}(R_{\theta})W$, and $B_{\theta}B = -\gamma_{0}^{2}(\cos\theta\,\gamma_{1} + \sin\theta\,\gamma_{2})\gamma_{1} = \cos\theta + \sin\theta\,\gamma_{1}\gamma_{2} = R_{\theta}^{2}/n$, the spin rotor whose $\mathrm{Ad}$ is the turn by $2\theta$ (checked at five Pythagorean half-angles with the double-angle action on $\gamma_{1}$). At $\theta = \pi$, $R_{\pi} = \gamma_{1}\gamma_{2}$, $B_{\pi} = -B$, $W_{\pi} = W'$ and $B_{\pi}B = -1$; at $\theta = 0$ the product is $1$. The path $\theta \mapsto \cos\theta + \sin\theta\,\gamma_{1}\gamma_{2}$, $\theta \in [0, \pi]$, is the lift starting at $1$ of the loop of turns by $2\theta$, a closed loop of rotations, and it ends at $-1$: the rotation by $2\pi$ of the spin group, $-1$ on spinor values and $(-1)^{2s}$ on spin-$s$ values. As maps $\mathrm{Ad}(B_{\pi}) = \mathrm{Ad}(-B) = \mathrm{Ad}(B)$, so the sign at $\theta = \pi$ is fixed only by the continuity of the lift. A form that does not depend on any choice of sign: $B_{\pi/2} = \gamma_{0}\gamma_{2}$ and $(\epsilon_{1}B_{\pi/2}\,\epsilon_{2}B)^{2} = (\gamma_{0}\gamma_{2}\gamma_{0}\gamma_{1})^{2} = (\gamma_{2}\gamma_{1})^{2} = -1$ for $\epsilon_{1}, \epsilon_{2} = \pm 1$, so the reflections of $W$ and of its quarter-turned copy compose to a rotor of the half turn whose square is the rotation by $2\pi$ in the spin group (checked for all four sign choices, with $\mathrm{Ad}$ of the product negating $\gamma_{1}$). In Kuckert's theorem the sign that matters is carried at the field level by the twist (iv). In Kuckert's notation $R(\varphi) = J_{\varphi/2}J_{W}$ \cite{Kuckert1995} (Corollary 3.2; Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-kuckert-modular-pct-spin-statistics-and-borchers-theorem}(i)), the product of the conjugations of the turned wedge and of $W$; (iii) is its geometric content: the product of the reflections is the lift of the rotation by $\varphi$, continuous in $\varphi$ and $-1$ at $\varphi = 2\pi$.

\emph{(iv).} This is the standard Klein-twist identity of the field net with $i$ written as $I_{4}$; the script represents the grading by even involutions of $\Cl(1,3)$ commuting with $I_{4}$ and the conjugate-linear $J$ by the reversal of $I_{4}$. $I_{4}$ is central in the even subalgebra, so a real span of $1$, $I_{4}$, $k$, $I_{4}k$ is commutative. With $k^{2} = 1$: $(1 + I_{4}k)^{2} = 1 + 2I_{4}k + I_{4}^{2}k^{2} = 2I_{4}k$ and $(1 + I_{4})^{2} = 2I_{4}$, so $V^{2} = k$; $(1 + I_{4})^{-1} = (1 - I_{4})/2$. The adjoint reverses the unit and fixes $k$: $V^{*} = (1 - I_{4}k)(1 - I_{4})^{-1}$, and $VV^{*} = (1 - I_{4}^{2}k^{2})/(1 - I_{4}^{2}) = 1$. A conjugate-linear $J$ reverses $I_{4}$ again and fixes $k$, so $JV^{*}J = V$ and $VJV^{*}J = V^{2} = k$. The script checks these for three even involutions $k$ commuting with $I_{4}$ and that $V \ne k$. This is the step $R(2\pi) = J_{\pi}J_{\mathcal{F}} = VJ_{\mathcal{F}}V^{*}J_{\mathcal{F}} = V^{2} = k$ of \cite{Kuckert1995} (Corollary 3.5), where $J_{\pi} = VJ_{\mathcal{F}}V^{*}$ comes from twisted duality, which Kuckert derives (from \cite{DoplicherRoberts1990}) rather than assumes, and $VJ_{\mathcal{F}} = J_{\mathcal{F}}V^{*}$; with the field theory's unit $I_{4}$ in place of $i$.

\emph{(v).} Imported: under Kuckert's Assumptions I to III (covering-group covariance with the spectrum condition, a unique cyclic vacuum, irreducibility, separability; modular P1CT symmetry $J_{W}\mathcal{A}(O)J_{W} = \mathcal{A}(j_{W}O)$ for double cones; a compact group of internal symmetries) in dimension $1 + s$, $s \ge 2$, every covariant normal field has $R(2\pi) = k$ \cite{Kuckert1995}; the paper notes that the modular groups need not act geometrically, so the premise is weaker than modular covariance, which implies it (Bisognano and Wichmann for Wightman fields \cite{BW1976}; Guido and Longo, Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-free-field-spin-statistics-and-guido-longo-theorem}(iii)). For the series' free fields the same sign is already fixed by locality with positive norm (\claimref{synthesis.locality-of-the-attached-free-fields-fixes-their-statistics}); the theorem matters for interacting fields.

\emph{(vi).} Argued. The premise has a translation part and an algebra part. The translation part follows by (ii) from the spectrum condition, which is a hypothesis of the theorem and is not supplied by the store for an interacting net: (N$_{+}$) concerns quasi-free states of a CAR mode algebra, and the positive conformal energy result concerns the representation on a given state's GNS space. The algebra part, $J_{W}\mathcal{A}(O)J_{W} = \mathcal{A}(j_{W}O)$ for all double cones, is not implied: Borchers' relations constrain $J_{W}$ only through its commutation with the translations, and the KMS property at period $2\pi$ for the boosts, which (N$_{+}$) gives for quasi-free states, identifies the modular group on the wedge algebra but says nothing about where $J_{W}$ sends the algebras of regions inside $W$ (and \claimref{synthesis.modular-period-on-values-is-the-dual-plane-turn} shows that KMS at $2\pi$ does not fix statistics). Neither (HS), a statement about two-point functions on generators, nor (HD), about the state's occupation profile, bears on it. The field net of the theorem carries charges localisable in double cones or spacelike cones; the electric charge, constrained by the Gauss law, is not localisable there, so the electron's spin-statistics connection beyond perturbation theory needs more than this premise. Transport-absent: the theorem is standard; the reading of the reflection as the PT inversion after the half modular period and the twist with the unit $I_{4}$ re-express it, as the stored modular-period result classifies its own $I_{4}$ reading.
